findings.issue: The automatic redispatch of a zero-tool reviewer calls dispatch() directly, from inside reviewer_session_step, which advance() runs BEFORE stored_green(..., 'gated'). The redispatch therefore writes a new reviewer brief (audit-lookup.py brief prints 'The recorded gate run' from task.testEvidence) without first asking verdict_basis whether that stored run still answers the gate. On the first dispatch the order is gate check then dispatch (stored_green / gate_step precede the dispatch at 3319); on this path it is dispatch then (after the reviewer files) gate check. If the gate entries or the tree moved while the first reviewer session ran, the second reviewer is shown a verdict P131.17 would have re-measured. The same bypass already exists in apply_answer's 'redispatch' (4602-4604) but that one is a human's act; this one is automatic. No case exercises it.
findings.resolution: In reviewer_unread, before dispatch(), ask stored_green(ctx, state, manifest, task, 'gated') (pass manifest through) and, when it returns STORED_MOVED, run gate_step first and return its stop; or spend the 'dispatched-reviewer' mark and return None so advance() reaches its own gate check before dispatching. Add a case that edits the task's gate between the first and second reviewer session and asserts the second brief is preceded by a re-measure.

findings.issue: Three branches the module docstring promises have no case: a stream the drive cannot count in (stream_tool_calls returns None, a stop 'of its own, never read as a count of none'), a session whose last message holds no JSON object (return_object None, falls to the plain no-reviewer-return decision), and submit refusing the object's shape (returns the refusal tuple). rv1-rv6 only reach the zero-tool, many-tool and no-session paths. The None-vs-0 distinction guards against reading an unreadable stream as 'opened nothing' or as 'opened something', and nothing would go red if it were collapsed.
findings.resolution: Add cases: a stream file with no assistant event (expect the 'cannot count tool calls' stop, no cannot-tell note, no redispatch); a tools>0 stream whose result text is prose (expect no-reviewer-return); a tools>0 stream whose JSON lacks verdict (expect the shape refusal and nothing filed).

findings.issue: This diff made dispatch() take the task's tree for a reviewer session (advance() now passes it, 3319), but the sibling call site that re-dispatches the reviewer after a no-reviewer-return decision still calls dispatch(ctx, state, phase, task, 'reviewer') with no tree. With writerModel set, that session would run with --tree set to the project rather than the member's own tree. apply_answer has no tree in scope today, so this may be unreachable for a wave member; nothing in the diff says so.
findings.resolution: Either pass the task's kept tree (kept_tree(state, task)) at 4604, or state in reviewer_dispatch's docstring that a redispatch from a decision always runs in the project tree and why that is right.

intent.note: Task: 'Reviewers run through run-agent-session.py with their agent body. The drive counts the reviewer session's tool calls from its saved stream; a return from a session with zero tool calls is recorded as cannot-tell and the reviewer is dispatched once more'. Diff: dispatch() routes role reviewer to reviewer_dispatch -> writer_argv(role='reviewer') (run-agent-session.py --role reviewer, which builds --agents from the agent body); stream_tool_calls counts tool_use blocks in assistant events; reviewer_unread notes cannot-tell on the task, files nothing, and redispatches once (MAX_REVIEWER_REDISPATCH=1). Acceptance (2) 'a second zero-tool return stops with a note instead of a third dispatch': the second branch returns _stopped naming both sessions. (3) a session with tool calls has its last message filed through submit and goes on. (4) the reviewer body is 6994 bytes by the cut I measured (frontmatter stripped), at or under 7000; the file net grew 9 bytes, so 'removing as many bytes elsewhere' is met only as 'stays under the ceiling'. 'Recorded as cannot-tell' is implemented as a task note plus no filed return, not as a filed intent answer; a reasonable reading that rv2 pins. The executor's claim (outcome, claims block) describes this diff accurately, including the P131.17 ordering statement: reviewer_session_step (3299-3305) runs before stored_green(...,'gated') (3310), and after a filed reviewer stored_green still runs and a MOVED mark re-measures (3311-3318). Nothing in the reviewer path shows a stored gate verdict: the wait, the unread note and the two stops carry session ids and stream names only, and no pending decision is created by it, so pending_still_applies / verdict_basis are not on its path. The filed return is read back through filed() (journal-row checked) and is not a verdict, so it is not reused past the stored_green check in any way the Agent path did not already. The one crossing is finding 1: the automatic redispatch writes a brief with the recorded gate run before that check.
